cards.issue_title: Loan form does not show what matters most by order or color
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks, filling the loan form does not by itself show which inputs matter most.
They wanted top-to-bottom to mean importance (how much money, then rate, then tenure) and left-to-right to mean column importance.
They said colors, sequence, and order should do that work so the user becomes “intelligent” without an explanation.
They said this may not be the most urgent change right now, but it should still be done.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, the Loan inputs form does not encode which fields matter most; they said filling it should make the user intelligent without explanation, using top-to-bottom importance (money, rate, tenure), left-to-right column importance, and colors/sequence/order.
cards.on_screen_object: Loan inputs form on Explore banks
quotes_sample: While filling this form, I become intelligent.
And this is the most important property, the tenure.
And you can use just colors and sequencing and order, right?
related_discussion_one_liners: Joke that the other person thinks they will be “hit” if they have to explain the form.
Later restated that people are trained left-to-right and up-to-down: “People usually train left to right. Up to down. We do the same.”
Tesla going to mass market, foolproof vs “full-proof,” and climbing from non-stupid to stupid sit with issue 04, not as a second form-layout defect.
Rate / amount / tenure as three affected outputs was already in progress in wb-rec-260815-2304.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the Loan inputs form not encoding field importance by top-to-bottom/left-to-right order, color, or sequence — not extra fields vanishing, not arranging (i) tooltips, and not extra words in site copy.

cards.issue_title: Extra eligibility fields should not vanish
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks they opened Adjust eligibility and said those extra fields should not disappear.
They said it is fine if the fields stay pre-filled.
They then set Co-applicant to No, and the extra co-applicant fields went away.
The object is the extra fields under Adjust eligibility, not the main loan card.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, extra fields under Adjust eligibility vanish (they said they should not disappear like that); pre-filled is acceptable. After Co-applicant No, the extra co-applicant fields are gone.
cards.on_screen_object: Adjust eligibility extra fields, including Co-applicant Yes/No
quotes_sample: That it should not disappear like this.
And there is no problem if it is pre-filled.
related_discussion_one_liners: Sits next to issue 01 (form order/color) but is a different object: visibility of extra fields, not ranking of main fields.
They did not say pre-filled values are dishonest.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is extra Adjust eligibility fields vanishing (including after Co-applicant No), not ranking main loan-card fields by order/color, not arranging info-icon tooltips, and not extra words raising cognitive load.

cards.issue_title: Loan form info icons need arranging
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks they pointed at the many (i) icons on the loan form.
They said to arrange all of those tooltips, then argued about whether to read them.
They opened Credit card limits, Tenure, and Existing EMIs.
The object is the info-icon tooltips on Loan inputs, not the field order.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, the (i) tooltips on the loan form need arranging; they said to arrange them, then opened Credit card limits, Tenure, and Existing EMIs instead of leaving the cluster as-is.
cards.on_screen_object: Info-icon tooltips on Loan inputs (Credit card limits, Tenure, Existing EMIs)
quotes_sample: Let's not read all the tooltips.
related_discussion_one_liners: They imagined most of the public as “stupid” and said details do not impress those people.
They talked about climbing a ladder from non-stupid to stupid and making the product foolproof — audience talk for why tooltips/copy must be simple, not a second tooltip defect.
Tesla / foolproof spelling sits with issue 04.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the (i) tooltip cluster on Loan inputs needing arranging (Credit card limits, Tenure, Existing EMIs), not field importance by order/color, not extra eligibility fields disappearing, and not extra words in quoted site copy.

cards.issue_title: Extra words in site copy raise cognitive load
summary_4_lines: They treated site sentences as too heavy: extra “no”s and extra clauses make people work harder.
They contrasted “Compare all and apply in one shot. And banks will compete for you” with the lighter “Compare and apply. Let banks compete.”
They also said stacked claims like Structure / No commission / No bias load too much context.
They looked up “cognitive load” on Google while the Explore banks form stayed on screen.
cards.pinpoint: Site sentences add extra words that raise cognitive load: repeating “no” (no x, no y, no z vs no x, y, z) and long CTAs (“Compare all and apply in one shot. And banks will compete for you” vs “Compare and apply. Let banks compete.”).
cards.on_screen_object: Site copy they quoted (Structure / No commission / No bias; Compare all and apply in one shot) discussed while Explore banks Loan inputs was on screen
quotes_sample: No x, no y, no z. This cognitive load has increased.
Compare all and apply in one shot. And banks will compete for you. The load has increased.
related_discussion_one_liners: Before the Google search: a “stupid” public, details that do not impress, and not worrying if some smart traffic arrives — why copy must stay light, not a separate page defect.
Climbing a ladder; foolproof vs “full-proof” / waterproof / airproof; Tesla going to mass market.
After the compare/apply contrast: training-data / PR-then-code analogy — models follow common instructions with less training.
They closed by saying people train left-to-right and up-to-down — the same principle as issue 01’s form order.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is extra words in quoted site sentences raising cognitive load (stacked “no”s and a long compare-and-apply CTA), not form-field ranking by order/color, not vanishing Adjust eligibility fields, and not arranging info-icon tooltips.
